messages:
anna_ops: Heads up — after the KMS key rotation last night our ingest service started failing with AccessDenied on Decrypt. Observed errors in app logs and CloudTrail. Anyone seen this pattern after rotation? :thinking_face:

matt_infra: Did the service assume a role to call KMS? Usually failures like that are either key policy denying the assumed-role ARN or a missing grant token when a grant was being used.

anna_ops: Yes, service runs as arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/ingest-role/session. We rotate keys via alias swap (alias/ingest-key -> new key), no change to the app. Logs show: 

```
An error occurred (AccessDeniedException) when calling the Decrypt operation: User: arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/ingest-role/session is not authorized to use KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:444455556666:key/abcd-ef01-2345
```

cj_security: CloudTrail capture of the KMS event? That message is the KMS side rejection. Two quick checks: 1) key policy grants to the IAM role (remember KMS checks key policy first), 2) any grants that existed might have been invalidated by rotation if they used grant tokens or were created against the previous key id.

kms-bot: CloudTrail event: {eventTime: "2024-09-02T03:12:34Z", eventName: "Decrypt", errorCode: "AccessDeniedException", kmsKeyId: "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:444455556666:key/abcd-ef01-2345"} 

matt_infra: Can you run `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/ingest-key` and paste output? If the list is empty, no grants exist. Also check `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/ingest-key --policy-name default` to verify the key policy allows the assumed role (or the account) to call Decrypt.

anna_ops: Ran those: list-grants returns empty. get-key-policy shows a statement that allows the account root and an explicit IAM role arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/kms-service to use the key, but NOT the ingest-role. We assumed the role-to-role trust before, but the policy never included the assumed-role ARN. Oops.

cj_security: That's the common trap: key policies should reference the principal that actually appears on the KMS request — which for cross-account or assumed-role flows is the assumed-role principal (the STS ARN), not the IAM role's role ARN. Two options: 1) add the role ARN (arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/ingest-role) to the key policy with kms:Decrypt, or 2) better — allow the account or the IAM role principal and use condition keys to restrict by source/Tag/EncryptionContext. Also consider aws:PrincipalTag conditions if you rely on session tags.

matt_infra: Also check encryption context: if the app includes EncryptionContext when encrypting and we require matching context on Decrypt via key policy condition, a missing or mismatched encryptionContext will yield AccessDenied. Can you run the decrypt from your laptop with verbose to reproduce? Example: 

```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://payload.bin --key-id alias/ingest-key --output text --debug
```

anna_ops: Tried the same via the assumed role and got the same AccessDenied. I also noticed we set session tags in the assume-role call earlier (service:ingest=true). Could the session tags be required in key policy condition? We do have one key policy condition that checks `StringEquals: {"aws:PrincipalTag/service": "ingest"}` — but session tags aren't being propagated?

cj_security: Session tags are only present on the principal if `sts:TagSession` was used when assuming the role OR the caller forwarded tags. If the app obtains temporary creds via an intermediate service that didn't pass tags through, the principal won't have tags and the condition will fail. Check CloudTrail AssumeRole call to see TagList.

kms-bot: Found AssumeRole event: `assumedRoleId: AIDA:ingest-session`, `sessionContext: attributes`: no session tags in request.

sre_oncall: That explains it — key policy condition requiring aws:PrincipalTag/service=ingest will block Decrypt for sessions without tags. Options: remove the tag condition, update the AssumeRole call to include `--tags Key=service,Value=ingest` or modify the trust/STS usage to pass tags. For a quick fix, add a temporary key policy statement allowing the specific assumed-role session ARN pattern `arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/ingest-role/*` to kms:Decrypt.

anna_ops: I added a permissive temporary statement to the key policy allowing the account 111122223333 and the assumed-role pattern. Retried decrypt — success :white_check_mark:.

cj_security: Long term we should: 1) avoid relying exclusively on session tags unless we guarantee they are set on every AssumeRole; 2) prefer key policy that grants the IAM role (role ARN) or account with least privilege conditions; 3) if you need grants (for service principals like CloudHSM or Lambda), create them and persist or recreate on rotation; 4) document rotation playbook to update any grant tokens and verify key policy statements reference stable principals.

matt_infra: I also recommend adding a smoke test in the rotation job that runs a Decrypt using the service's assumed-role credentials immediately after alias swap. If it fails, roll back alias and alert.

anna_ops: Will implement the smoke test and remove the temporary policy change once we switch to tagging on AssumeRole calls. Thanks all. :pray:
